## Unit of Work

- Default: `IUnitOfWork` is the commit boundary of an Application use case — repositories stage changes and do not call `SaveChangesAsync` independently; Application Services decide when the operation commits. Infrastructure implements `IUnitOfWork` over the application's `DbContext`.
- Repositories participating in one use case must share the same scoped Unit of Work and `DbContext`. Inject repositories explicitly into their consumers; `IUnitOfWork` must not become a repository container or service locator exposing repositories as properties.
- Default: no explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case needs control beyond a normal `SaveChangesAsync`.

One `SaveChangesAsync` is the transaction boundary for one application operation. An explicit transaction fits a concrete use case where several database operations or several `SaveChangesAsync` calls succeed or fail together. EF transaction APIs do not solve distributed transactions.

| Scenario | Technique |
|---|---|
| Read-only entity query | `AsNoTracking()` when useful |
| Read model | Database-side projection |
| Primary-key entity lookup | `FindAsync` when its semantics fit |
| Complex entity graph | Explicit `Include` / projection |
| Set-based mass update/delete | `ExecuteUpdateAsync` / `ExecuteDeleteAsync` when appropriate |
| Normal query | Ordinary LINQ |
| Measured extremely hot query | Consider a compiled query |
| Several commits that succeed or fail together | Explicit transaction |
| Production schema change | Reviewed migration, controlled deployment step |
| Empty development database | Run the maintained development seeder |
| Fresh local seed dataset needed | Recreate the local database explicitly |
| Test data | Dedicated test setup (`dotnet-testing`) |

Do not wrap normal EF Core operations in a generic application-level retry pipeline. When the provider supports transient retry through EF Core execution strategies or provider configuration, prefer that, and handle transaction/retry interaction according to the provider's EF Core guidance. HTTP retry policies are not database policies.

|---|---|
| External I/O | Bounded execution time |
| Safe transient HTTP failure | Consider retry |
| Unsafe write | No retry unless duplicate-safe |
| `429` from dependency | Honor `Retry-After` where appropriate |
| Repeated dependency outage | Consider circuit breaker |
| Optional data unavailable | Consider explicit fallback |
| Latency-sensitive idempotent read | Consider hedging after measurement |
| EF transient faults | Provider/EF execution strategy |
| Incoming request rate limiting | ASP.NET Core rate limiter |

context_quotes:
- Default: caching is an optimization, not an architecture requirement. Introduce it only for a clear measured or reasoned need — expensive repeated work, high read volume, expensive remote calls with acceptable staleness — and choose the implementation by deployment, consistency and staleness requirements, never merely because a value is read often.
- Cache technology must stay out of Domain, and infrastructure cache APIs must not leak into Application without a deliberate boundary abstraction.
- Cache keys must uniquely represent the cached value and include every relevant dimension (identifier, tenant, user when user-specific, locale, query parameters); avoid global keys for user- or tenant-specific data.

- **HTTP response caching** — ASP.NET Core output caching when the whole response can safely be reused; it belongs in the API layer.
- **Application/data caching** — when a use case genuinely needs cache-aware behavior, define an Application abstraction and implement it in Infrastructure; skip the abstraction when caching can stay an internal Infrastructure concern.
- **Infrastructure caching** — adapters may cache expensive remote or persistence operations when the contract exposed to Application is preserved.

Infrastructure may implement it with `HybridCache`, which stays out of Application contracts (`rules/backend/caching.md`). Centralize key construction once duplicated key formats become hard to maintain.
